candidate_source_code: 9a2e747 (includes PR #67 closed-waiter fix; does not include independent PR #68 shared-channel fix)
scope: Controlled Linux loopback on a second owner-provided host with four online vCPUs and exposed crypto acceleration; this is not a WAN measurement.

workload.fault: one test-only TCP proxy pauses server-to-client forwarding for 6 seconds

measurement.helper: quality-probe-v4; standalone Go standard-library echo load generator
measurement.quantiles: Nearest rank ceil(n*p)-1, computed separately per run; summary reports median of those per-run quantiles.
measurement.failure_latencies: All-attempt quantiles include elapsed wall time for failed attempts. Successful-only p95/p99 fields remain for comparison.
measurement.skipped_demand: The scheduled probe that finds all four concurrency slots occupied increments probe_skipped_at_concurrency_cap; it is not silently omitted.
measurement.throughput: Measured successful payload bytes per elapsed time at a fixed 20 Mbit/s offered application load, not maximum tunnel capacity.
measurement.asset_transfer: Temporary peer HTTP transfer with archive and uncompressed executable SHA-256 checks before extraction/execution; the file server was stopped before trials and both temporary directories were removed.

limitations: Three short runs per revision on one four-vCPU loopback host do not establish production/WAN equivalence or absence of quality regression.
There are fewer failed probes and a lower median per-run p99, but candidate sample 2 has p99 205.516 ms, worse than every baseline sample.
Median per-run p95 is 2.971 ms for candidate versus 2.681 ms for baseline; no p95 improvement is claimed.
The same-host no-fault control is recorded separately in wssmux-modern-control-2026-11-12.json; do not pool the workloads.
One engine uses GOMAXPROCS=1; client and server are separate processes sharing the host with the echo/proxy/load fixture and existing services.
Do not pool samples with the earlier host or profile results; hardware and workload differ.
Production services and kernel-wide policies were not changed. Existing streams cannot migrate between carriers.
